---
title: "Research Specialisations"
---

## A. Causal foundation models

Combine causal identification, structural priors and foundation-model architectures.

## B. Learning mechanisms

Study mechanisms whose allocation/payment rules are learned while respecting incentive, feasibility and welfare constraints.

## C. Economic and AI agents

Study artificial agents in auctions, bargaining, markets, public-goods problems and platforms.

## D. Economically structured foundation models

Embed restrictions such as monotonicity, adding-up, revealed preference, equilibrium or incentive compatibility into learned architectures.

## E. Relational economic foundation models

Treat economic relationships—choice, trade, matching, platform membership—as structured edges rather than generic database links.
